name_reason: Follows data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> with domain=battle and a fully semantic descriptor (cursor_screen_y = cursor row within viewport). _y is a meaningful axis suffix, not a Ghidra address residue. It belongs to the cohesive viewport/cursor family in cursor.c whose 6 siblings are all data_fd2_battle_* (origin_x/y, cursor_world_x/y, cursor_screen_x); per the same-file/same-kind naming-consistency rule the battle prefix must stay even though the viewport is also driven in field-walk/cutscene contexts (same engine subsystem). Referenced byte-identical across 14 src files + globals.h.
purpose: Runtime battle/field cursor row within the on-screen viewport (0-based screen tile row of the cursor).
logic_summary: SIGNED int scalar (4 bytes), zero at load (BSS). Cleared to 0 by fd2_init_battle_state_for_chapter (MOV dword [0x53ABD],0 @ 0x2064B) and set from the save header via MOVZX byte->dword in save-load (@ 0x10415). Thereafter INC/DEC by the cursor-move (fd2_cursor_move_up/down) and walk-step functions. The up/down handlers compare it with SIGNED branches: CMP [0x53ABD],2 / JGE (scroll-up edge, @0x11B5B/0x11B62) and CMP [0x53ABD],5 / JLE (step-down edge, @0x11BB3/0x11BBA). It legitimately goes negative when a cinematic walk reaches the map top (origin_y hits 0 disables the scroll branch, inner branch keeps decrementing), which is why a signed declaration is required for a faithful JGE/JLE match.
element_semantics: Single scalar: 0-based row of the cursor within the on-screen viewport (8-tile-tall window). Normal range ~0..7 but can go negative during a top-edge cinematic walk; signedness is load-bearing.
notes: Verified all comment claims against ground truth: (1) signed JGE/JLE branches confirmed by disasm of fd2_cursor_move_up @0x11B48 (CMP [0x53ABD],2;JGE) and fd2_cursor_move_down @0x11B9B (CMP [0x53ABD],5;JLE); (2) init zero-write confirmed at 0x2064B (C705 BD3A0500 00000000); (3) save-load MOVZX byte->dword write confirmed at 0x10415 (0FB64608 / A3 BD3A0500). is_const=false: many game writers (init, save-load, cursor/walk handlers). Existing src comment block (cursor.c lines 334-355) and Ghidra plate are both accurate and mutually consistent (same signed rationale + chapter-1 prologue bottom-scroll bug); left untouched. No logic issues found.
